description: A design where a container, not your code, decides when objects are created and how they are connected.
An ordinary object that the Spring container creates, wires and manages, declared by a stereotype or a bean method.
The Spring container that holds the beans, injects their dependencies and manages their lifecycle.
The search of the application class package and its sub-packages for classes with stereotype annotations.
Passing dependencies as constructor parameters so fields stay final and the class works without Spring in tests.
An annotation that narrows type-matching beans by qualifier value; several beans can share the same value.
The rule for how many instances of a bean exist: one per container for singleton, a new one per request for prototype.
